description:
Establish the addressable documentation contract and enforcement baseline that all rewrite, archival and tersification work must satisfy. This checkpoint makes the project's documentation rules explicit, reviewable, projected into operational guidance, and mechanically checked.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-31: The JIT item-kind registry supports project-scoped addressable invariants with stable `@/inv/<id>` resolution and an `enforces` linkage namespace.
- [hard] REQ-32: An approved invariant registry covers three documentation rule groups: (a) comments and rustdoc carry only non-obvious content in the shortest form, with a module orientation of at most one short paragraph and no duplication; (b) documentation states current behavior and limits only, with no speculation, future promises, non-goals or deferrals; (c) rustdoc examples are non-trivial, active development documents live under `dev/active/<epic-short-id>-<slug>/` linked to their owning issues, and every `AGENTS.md` respects its recursive scope and 200-line limit.
- [hard] REQ-33: Invariants are projected into a delimited region of the authoritative root `AGENTS.md`; projection is deterministic and leaves hand-authored content outside the region unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-34: The root `AGENTS.md` defines recursive scope and the crate-local override convention, remains at or below 200 lines, and `CLAUDE.md` is a repository symlink to it.
- [hard] REQ-35: The `doc-review` gate is an automated, issue-scoped review grounded in `AGENTS.md` and the addressable invariant registry; it cites the invariant addresses it applies, and its rubric evaluates accuracy, canonical placement, research relevance, aggregate concision, current-state prose, evidence, and example value. Issue-attributable violations block; untouched pre-existing text is advisory.
- [hard] REQ-36: A `docs-mechanical` gate checks Markdown links and anchors, repository-local citations, addressable-item citations, and invariant/rule/gate projection freshness over a documentation footprint read from configuration. The footprint covers permanent documentation (root and crate READMEs, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), Markdown under `dev/active/`, and repository-relative links in Rust doc comments.
- [hard] REQ-37: Documentation checks have committed self-tests covering clean inputs, each supported failure class, environment errors, and projection drift without encoding a hand-maintained inventory of product facts.
- [hard] REQ-38: The Rust CI gate builds rustdoc in release mode with warnings denied and runs doctests, each as a separately reported step, and GitHub CI runs the same steps.
- [hard] REQ-40: `jit invariant check`, invariant projection, documentation review, documentation mechanical checks, and JIT validation all pass together on the established baseline.

## Decisions

- DEC-01: The migration-manifest schema and transient progress checker (former REQ-39) belong to the epic's migration work, not to this contract. Requirement IDs REQ-31 to REQ-40 avoid collision with the epic's REQ-01 to REQ-20 under subtree-wide coverage credit.
- DEC-02: Researcher-audience, adapted Diátaxis placement and no-marketing invariants are registered with the permanent-documentation rewrite, where placement first applies, not in this story.
- DEC-03: The new invariant texts are drafted in a linked document and approved by the user in one interview round before registration and projection.
- DEC-04: `doc-review` keeps its existing AI-review wrapper and reviewer; only its prompt changes.
- DEC-05: `docs-mechanical` is a stdlib-only Python script under `contrib/gates/` with fixture-based self-tests; it delegates JIT-specific checks to `jit item show` and projection rendering.
- DEC-06: Rustdoc build and doctests run inside `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` rather than as a separate gate.

## Notes

This story defines the prerequisite contract. It does not migrate historical documents or author the new permanent documentation corpus.
title: Define documentation contract and enforcement baseline
